edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff’s First Requests for Production. This revised draft proposes the procedures and deadlines below. It does not represent that collection or review is complete. The request-specific supplemental responses will state the scope of production and whether responsive material is being withheld for each request.
edits.name: Preliminary statement

edits.text: 1. REQUEST-SPECIFIC RESPONSES. Defendant withdraws the blanket general objection. Within seven calendar days after agreement to this proposed timetable, Defendant will serve a separate supplemental response to each request identifying any specific objection and its basis, describing the portion of the request Defendant will answer, and stating whether responsive material is being withheld on that objection. Each response will distinguish documents not located after a reasonable search from documents withheld. If a request remains disputed, Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged material within the undisputed scope on the schedule below.
edits.name: Request-specific responses

edits.text: 2. PRODUCTION SCHEDULE, SEARCH SCOPE, AND FORMAT. Defendant proposes beginning production within 14 calendar days after agreement to this timetable and completing production within 30 calendar days after that agreement. Within seven calendar days after agreement, Defendant will identify the proposed custodians, relevant date ranges, repositories, and search methodology for discussion, including reasonably accessible email, shared drives, local files, messaging platforms, and paper files reasonably likely to contain responsive material. Defendant will identify proposed exclusions and their reasons rather than treat them as agreed. Defendant proposes searchable, Bates-numbered PDFs for ordinary documents, native files for spreadsheets and other files whose usability would be materially impaired by PDF conversion, and a metadata load file for electronically stored information. Document families will be maintained, and redactions will be identified by basis. Any anticipated delay will be raised promptly, with its reason and a proposed revised completion date.
edits.name: Production and search protocol

edits.text: 3. PRIVILEGE LOG. No privilege log accompanied the prior draft; the statement that one was attached is withdrawn. Defendant proposes serving a privilege log with each production for responsive material then withheld or redacted on privilege or work-product grounds, with a complete log due by the proposed production-completion deadline. The log will identify the applicable request, document identifier, date, author, recipients and their roles where relevant, document type, a non-privileged description of the subject matter, and the asserted protection and its basis sufficiently to permit assessment without disclosing protected information. Any proposed categorical treatment or exclusion from logging will be identified for agreement or resolution under applicable rules.
edits.name: Privilege log correction

edits.text: 4. SUPPLEMENTATION AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Defendant will supplement its responses and production as required by applicable rules. The parties should confer promptly regarding disputed requests, search scope, production format, or privilege claims. No proposed search limitation, logging exclusion, or extension will be treated as accepted merely because it appears in this draft. These proposals do not waive either party’s rights.
edits.name: Supplementation and disputes
